claims.text: Variations in Mn content cause element-specific changes in local stacking-fault energy.
Variations in Mn content modify magnetic interactions in these FCC alloys.
Mn-induced changes in stacking-fault energy and magnetic interactions shift the balance between dislocation slip and nano-twinning.
Changes in the balance between dislocation slip and nano-twinning produce the mechanical-property differences among the quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloys.
The compared quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloys are equiatomic, single-phase FCC materials prepared by identical thermomechanical processing.
Mn content will be varied through the selection of equiatomic quaternary and ternary compositions.
Testing will use room-temperature tensile loading at a fixed strain rate with nominally uniform grain size and microstructure.
Mn-dependent local stacking-fault energy and magnetic interactions directly influence dislocation activity, twin formation, and possible FCC-to-HCP transformation.
The quinary alloy has an optimal Mn level that balances dislocation slip and nano-twinning.
The proposed balance of slip and nano-twinning in the quinary alloy enhances ductility and strain hardening.
Mn-reduced quaternary and ternary alloys have a higher effective stacking-fault energy than the quinary baseline.
Higher effective stacking-fault energy suppresses nano-twinning and favors dislocation slip.
Suppression of nano-twinning in the Mn-reduced alloys leads to lower strain hardening and ductility.
Relative to the quinary baseline, Mn-reduced quaternary and ternary alloys will show reduced nano-twinning and more slip-dominated deformation.
Relative to the quinary baseline, Mn-reduced quaternary and ternary alloys will exhibit lower strain hardening and damage tolerance.
Identical processing and testing conditions make compositional Mn variation the primary cause of observed differences.
Dislocation nucleation events and twin formation observed by in situ TEM can be used to map local stacking-fault energy indirectly.
A lack of systematic variation in stacking-fault energy, deformation mechanisms, and mechanical properties with Mn content would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis treats equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets generally as Mn-reduced. An equiatomic Mn-containing quaternary has 25 at.% Mn and an equiatomic Mn-containing ternary has about 33.3 at.% Mn, both greater than the quinary's 20 at.% Mn; only subsets that omit Mn have reduced Mn. The specific subsets are not identified, so the stated Mn-reduction trend is not consistently defined.
